# The single source of truth for AFD deployment shapes. One row = one vLLM
# process. `afd_launch.sh` derives everything else from these rows, so A, F,
# --data-parallel-size, --data-parallel-start-rank and --headless cannot drift
# out of agreement with each other.
# Columns (whitespace-separated):
#   scenario   name passed to afd_launch.sh
#   proc       unique process id within the scenario; also the log file name
#   role       attention | ffn
#   host       host SLOT, not an address. afd_launch.sh maps slots to real
#              addresses via HOSTS="h0=10.0.0.1 h1=10.0.0.2"; unmapped slots
#              default to 127.0.0.1, which is what makes single-host scenarios
#              need no configuration at all.
#   dp_local   data-parallel engines this process runs (--data-parallel-size-local)
#   tp         tensor-parallel size (--tensor-parallel-size); must be equal
#              across every process of the same role
#   gpus       CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES for this process, host-local device ids.
#              Must list exactly dp_local * tp devices.
# Derived by afd_launch.sh, never written here:
#   dp_size       = sum of dp_local over the role's rows
#   dp_start_rank = sum of dp_local over the role's PRECEDING rows, so ROW ORDER
#                   DEFINES RANK ORDER. The role's first row owns DP rank 0.
#   A, F          = dp_size * tp, per role
#   AFD_HOST      = address of the host slot on the ffn row with dp_start_rank 0
#   DP_ADDRESS    = address of the host slot on that role's dp_start_rank 0 row
#   --headless    = set on every row whose dp_start_rank is not 0
# Runtime knobs are NOT in this table on purpose: MODE=eager|graph, DBO,
# MODEL_PATH, MAX_NUM_SEQS and friends are environment variables, so any
# scenario can be run in any mode without duplicating rows.
# scenario              proc    role        host    dp_local  tp  gpus
# Smallest shape that exercises the connector. 2 GPUs.
1a1f                    attn0   attention   h0      1         1   0
1a1f                    ffn0    ffn         h0      1         1   1
# 4 GPUs. Equivalent to 2a2f_eager_dbo_dp2tp1.sh.
2a2f-dp2tp1             attn0   attention   h0      2         1   0,1
2a2f-dp2tp1             ffn0    ffn         h0      2         1   2,3
# 4 GPUs, parallelism inside each rank instead of across ranks.
# Equivalent to 2a2f_eager_dbo_dp1tp2.sh.
2a2f-dp1tp2             attn0   attention   h0      1         2   0,1
2a2f-dp1tp2             ffn0    ffn         h0      1         2   2,3
# 8 GPUs. Equivalent to 4a4f_eager_dbo_dp2tp2.sh.
4a4f-dp2tp2             attn0   attention   h0      2         2   0,1,2,3
4a4f-dp2tp2             ffn0    ffn         h0      2         2   4,5,6,7
# 6 GPUs, ratio 2: each FFN rank fans in from two Attention ranks.
4a2f-ratio2             attn0   attention   h0      4         1   0,1,2,3
4a2f-ratio2             ffn0    ffn         h0      2         1   4,5
# One role per host, 2 GPUs each. This is the shape verified on OpenShift on
# 2026-09-08, and the issue #327 "placement B" that succeeds: both FFN ranks
# share one network namespace, so only FFN rank 0 ever binds AFD_HOST.
2a2f-two-host           attn0   attention   h0      2         1   0,1
2a2f-two-host           ffn0    ffn         h1      2         1   0,1
# Issue #327 "placement C": the FFN role is split across hosts, so FFN rank 1
# tries to bind AFD_HOST -- an address it does not own -- and fails. Expect
# OSError: [Errno 99] before PR #328, and a healthy endpoint after it.
2a2f-split-ffn          attn0   attention   h0      2         1   1,2
2a2f-split-ffn          ffn0    ffn         h0      1         1   0
2a2f-split-ffn          ffn1    ffn         h1      1         1   0
# The mirror image: the Attention role is split across hosts instead. Both FFN
# ranks stay together, so this succeeds on either side of PR #328. Run it beside
# 2a2f-split-ffn to show that only the split role differs.
2a2f-split-attn         attn0   attention   h0      1         1   1
2a2f-split-attn         attn1   attention   h1      1         1   1
2a2f-split-attn         ffn0    ffn         h0      2         1   0,2
# Fully split: one rank per process, four host slots. On Kubernetes this is one
# pod per rank, which is the closest match to the EKS setup in issue #327.
2a2f-four-proc          attn0   attention   h0      1         1   0
2a2f-four-proc          attn1   attention   h1      1         1   0
2a2f-four-proc          ffn0    ffn         h2      1         1   0
2a2f-four-proc          ffn1    ffn         h3      1         1   0
